**Continuous 2.6.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.6.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.6.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.6.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.6.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.6.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.6.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.6.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.6.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.6.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.6.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.6.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.4.4

**Loop mode**

- **Build a plan in a loop.** A plan card's **Build in a loop** runs the plan's to-dos one at a time, each in a fresh context with a one-item prompt. The model's questions go to an inbox above the input, where you answer them while the work goes on; an answer is steered into a running item at its next tool boundary. When a round runs dry, the loop re-plans in a read-only Plan turn. (#315)
- **Loop is a mode.** It sits in the IDE's mode picker and in the CLI's Shift+Tab, ← and → cycle. The first message plans, the loop starts once the plan is presented, and leaving Loop stops after the running item. (#331)
- **How much it does on its own** is one setting with three levels, Supervised, Auto and Unattended, picked from the approval mode and changeable from the inbox. Each has budgets for rounds, tokens and time, editable while the loop runs. The loop stops when done, out of budget, after two rounds without progress or three failed items in a row, or on Stop. (#315, #331)
- **Controls and strategies.** Skip an item, run an item again, re-plan never, up to N times or until done. Three strategies: Finish what you started, Check in (a re-plan every three finished items) and Fix forward (a failed item gets re-plans of its own). (#331)
- **Plan files carry per-item lines** indented under a to-do: `after: 1, 2` for the steps it waits for, `check:` for a command that proves it, and `model: <name>` to run that item on another of your chat models, shown on the item's row. (#331, #364)
- **Notes between items.** `finish_item` takes notes handed to later items, an inbox note marked **For every item** rides with every later prompt, and a `remind_me` tool saves a note for one later run. An item can finish as `later` when another item may settle it. (#315, #331)
- **In the CLI and `cn serve`**, the same loop: **Build in a loop** on the plan prompt, `/loop` opens the inbox, a strip above the prompt shows the loop's state, and `cn serve` exposes it on `GET /state` and `POST /message` (`loopAnswer`, `loopAction`, `loopAutonomy`, `loopStrategy`, `loopBudget`). (#331)
- **Checks mean something.** A to-do whose check only tests that a file or string exists is flagged when the plan is presented; "done" means the item's check exited 0; a re-plan that changes the check of a stuck item is held for you. `remind_me` no longer refuses a note without `when`. (#365, pending)

**Modes and plans**

- **Decisions on a plan.** A choice you kept for yourself, or a costly one, becomes a decision on the plan instead of an assumption: options and a pick, written in the plan file, asked in the CLI before Build, and answerable in place on the IDE's plan card, which tells Build what was decided. (#356)
- **One set of turn texts** for Plan and Agent serves the IDE and the CLI. A refused tool call carries on instead of retrying, a model that names the next step and stops is nudged once, repeated identical calls are refused, and the task list block stays out of Plan turns. (#356)
- **Plan mode offers no task list tool in the IDE**, matching the CLI, so small models present the plan instead of writing a list. (#361, pending)
- Cut-off tool calls are refused and the model is asked to write in parts rather than run with repaired arguments; `create_new_file` takes `append`. (#315)

**Which model, which prompt**

- `modeModels` now covers `loop`, `replan`, `reviewer` and `subagent` as well as the modes, each with its own `reasoningEffort`. (#356)
- `modeModels.<use>.prompt` picks the system prompt for a use: `full`, `short`, `tailored`, or the name of a block under `prompts:`. Without it the model id decides: the tailored text for the Qwen coder and MoE models, the short text for other Qwen models, the full text otherwise. (#356, #359, #366)
- `rulesByMode.loop` and `rulesByMode.replan`, with matching switches in Settings > Rules. (#359)
- `modeModels.<use>.tail`: a one-line reminder at the end of your messages, on for Loop items and the short profile by default, `off`, or a text of your own. It leaves the system prompt alone so the cache holds. (#362, pending)
- **Settings > Models > Which model does what** gains Prompt and Reminder rows under Reasoning effort. (#369, pending)
- CLI subagents and `continuous review` run as their own use: a subagent's system message and no tail. (#368, pending)

**Policies and permissions**

- A workspace config file may add deny and ask rules, but not allow rules or reviewer guidance. (#356)
- The CLI's file tools refuse writes outside the working directory in headless runs and label them in interactive approvals. (#356)
- `cn serve` binds to loopback by default and needs a token to listen anywhere else. (#356)
- In a loop, a call that would ask is held as an approval question instead of stalling; **Allow once** grants that file or command. (#315, #331)

**Models and providers**

- **Amazon Bedrock, by model family:** reasoning fields for Claude, Nova 2, Qwen3 and DeepSeek V3.2, Claude's sampling constraints, tool support for every Nova, Mistral and Qwen3 model, non-streaming tool routes for Llama 4 and Qwen3 32B, Nova's thinking shown as reasoning, a retry without the cross-region prefix for on-demand-only ids, and prices for the other families (estimates are marked). (#356)
- **Bedrock setup** shows which models the account can use and caches the catalog for an hour, warns on bare ids, says when Anthropic models need the use-case form, and when Bedrock refuses a model the error says what to check (the tokens-per-minute quota, the form, the agreement). (#351, #352, #356)
- Claude on Bedrock no longer rejects a conversation with a cancelled tool call. (#353)
- Bedrock accounts: the API key is saved, and access keys go to secret storage instead of `models.yaml`. (#350, #355)
- Nova 2 Lite gets low reasoning effort by default; without it the plan turn deliberated in text and never called a tool. (#361, pending)
- Anthropic direct: never temperature with top_p, neither while thinking. OpenAI-compatible servers get `extraBodyProperties`, `top_k` and `min_p`. (#356)

**Prompt caching and cost**

- **Cache points for Amazon Nova** (2 Lite, Pro, Lite, Micro) in the system prompt and messages, on by default in the CLI; the chat window's cache button shows for Nova with a 5-minute lifetime and Nova prices. (#356; #360, pending)
- **A prefix that stays cached**: the per-process marker, the date and the git status are out of the system prefix, the system message is built once per mode, a loop's plan block sits after the item prompt, and the Anthropic cache marker no longer rides on the changing task list block. (#331, #356; #360, pending)
- **CLI accounting**: every total counts processed input (uncached, cache read and cache write), `cached_tokens` is read, `cn serve` sends one system message, and truncated replies are reported. (#331, #356)

**CLI and `cn serve`**

- A new startup banner, the Continuous loop and wordmark, sized to the terminal. (#345)
- The CLI stays at the input after the intro; packaged builds of 2.4.3 and 2.4.4 exited at once. (#349)
- `cn serve` holds Plan-turn questions in an inbox (`/state` `pendingQuestions`, answered with `POST /message { answerQuestion, answer }`); headless runs have no Exit tool; the Bash tool names its shell. (#356)

**VS Code integration**

- **The agent uses the language servers.** A `code_navigation` tool finds symbols, outlines a file, jumps to a definition, lists references and reports problems, read-only and without asking. After an edit, the tool result names the errors and warnings the edit introduced. (#346)
- **Your config files in the editor.** `config.yaml`, `models.yaml` and `providers.yaml` each get their own schema, problems show where they are as you type (an unknown `from:` with "did you mean", an account that does not exist, duplicate names), and model and account names are offered after `from:`, `model:` and `connection:`. (#348)
- **The whole model catalog in VS Code's model picker**, each variant on its own, marked as running on your own account, and the extension declares itself for the Agents window.
- **Accounts from VS Code's Language Models editor**, behind `continuous.accountsFromVSCode` (off by default, experimental): the key stays in VS Code's secret storage and the account is never written to a file.

**Benchmark and evaluation**

- `bench/`: a model benchmark runner over `cn serve` with 23 scenarios, a scorer and a comparison table. (#358)
- `npm run eval:turns` in `core`: a regression eval for the Plan and Agent turn texts by profile, with a fixed quality bar. (#361, pending)
- The tail reminder measured on Nova 2 Lite and Qwen3 Coder 30B; the built-in texts stay. (#367, #370, pending)

**Docs and fixes**

- The reference gains `modeModels` (with `prompt`), `rulesByMode` and the Bedrock and prompt caching pages are brought up to date; the roadmap adds tracks H to L with plans for the benchmark, context visibility and the codebase index. (#356, #357)
- Marketplace publishing can re-run for the platforms a release missed; CI no longer fails on downloads; every text file checks out as LF. (#343, #347, #354)
- The unused language client and its vulnerable `minimatch` are gone. (#344)

## Upgrading

Your configuration keeps working; the new `config.yaml` keys are optional:

- `modeModels.loop`, `.replan`, `.reviewer`, `.subagent`, and `modeModels.<use>.prompt` (`full`, `short`, `tailored` or a `prompts:` block), `modeModels.<use>.tail` (pending) and `rulesByMode.loop` / `.replan`. See `modeModels` in the [reference](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/reference).
- Qwen models now get the short or tailored turn text by model id. Set `modeModels.<use>.prompt: full` to keep the full text.
- Prompt caching is on by default for Amazon Nova on Bedrock in Agent and Plan modes and in the CLI. Set `promptCaching: false` on the model to turn it off.
- A Bedrock account set up with an API key on an earlier version saved no key: open it in provider setup and enter the key again. Access keys saved earlier stay in `models.yaml` until you save that account again. (#350, #355)
- Allow rules and reviewer guidance in a workspace `.continuous/config.yaml` are ignored now; put them in your user config. `cn serve` listens on loopback unless given a token. (#356)

## Known issues

- Nova 2 Lite under the plan turn: with reasoning off it writes its deliberation as text and never presents the plan; with the new default it meets the bar in most runs, not all. Loops on Nova often end an item without `finish_item` and rely on the nudge. (#361, #367, pending)
- Claude 5.x on Bedrock: on the account used for testing, the tokens-per-minute quota for the Claude 5.x models is 0 and AWS has not raised it, so they could not be tested live. The error names the quota, but only AWS can change it. (#351, #357)
- Qwen3 Coder on Bedrock sometimes writes a tool call as text; the turn then ends with no call and no nudge. Bedrock reports no cache reads for Qwen. (#370, pending)
- The CLI does not apply `modeModels.<use>.reasoningEffort`; set the effort on the model or pick a catalog variant. `modeModels.subagent` does not apply in the CLI, where a subagent is a model with the `subagent` role. (#368, pending)
- The Agents window and the accounts from VS Code's Language Models editor have not been tested in a real Agents window; both depend on proposed VS Code APIs that can change without notice.
- Loop's `later` deferral and blocking questions were only exercised by scripted models.
- Bedrock Mantle, and accounts whose use-case form was filed at the organization level, may see a wrong "needs use-case form" notice. It blocks nothing. (#352)

## Not included

The JetBrains plugin and the hosted Continue Hub are not part of Continuous. Hub `uses: owner/name` blocks are not supported; configure models and blocks directly or with local file paths.
